By Kakutani’s product-measure criterion, \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) are equivalent. Indeed, only the coordinates \(3k\) and \(3k+1\) matter, and

\[
(\sqrt{a_k}-\sqrt{b_k})^2\asymp \frac1{k^2(\log k)^2},\qquad
(\sqrt{b_k}-\sqrt{c_k})^2\asymp \frac1{k^2},
\]

both summable, while the \((\sqrt{1-p}-\sqrt{1-q})^2\) parts are even smaller and summable.

For one Bernoulli coordinate with \(\mu(1)=p,\nu(1)=q\),

\[
\int \left(\frac{d\mu}{d\nu}\right)^z\,d\nu
=
p^zq^{1-z}+(1-p)^z(1-q)^{1-z}.
\]

Thus

\[
M(z)=\prod_{k\ge3} A_k(z)B_k(z),
\]

where

\[
A_k(z)=a_k^zb_k^{1-z}+(1-a_k)^z(1-b_k)^{1-z},
\]

\[
B_k(z)=b_k^zc_k^{1-z}+(1-b_k)^z(1-c_k)^{1-z}.
\]

For real \(t\), the decisive terms are

\[
a_k^t b_k^{1-t}
=
k^{t-3}(\log k)^{-2t},
\]

and

\[
b_k^t c_k^{1-t}
=
k^{-t-2}.
\]

The remaining linear and quadratic corrections are summable because \(a_k,b_k,c_k\) are all summable. Therefore

\[
\sum_k(A_k(t)-1)<\infty
\iff
\sum_k k^{t-3}(\log k)^{-2t}<\infty
\iff t\le 2,
\]

with \(t=2\) attained since \(\sum k^{-1}(\log k)^{-4}<\infty\). Also

\[
\sum_k(B_k(t)-1)<\infty
\iff
\sum_k k^{-t-2}<\infty
\iff t>-1,
\]

and \(t=-1\) is not attained since then the decisive term is \(\sum k^{-1}\).

Hence

\[
\mathcal I=(-1,2].
\]

For complex \(z\), the product converges locally uniformly exactly on the maximal open vertical strip

\[
-1<\Re z<2,
\]

so \(M(z)\) is holomorphic there and represented by the above product.

Finally,

\[
\mathcal P_\nu=\{p>0:M(p)<\infty\}=(0,2],
\]

and

\[
\mathcal P_\mu
=
\left\{p>0:\int Z^{-p}\,d\mu<\infty\right\}
=
\{p>0:M(1-p)<\infty\}
=
(0,2).
\]

Also,

\[
Z^{-1}\in L^p(\nu)
\iff M(-p)<\infty
\iff 0<p<1.
\]

So the requested tuple is

\[
\boxed{\bigl((-1,2],\ (0,2],\ (0,2)\bigr)}.
\]
